First, U.S. wholesale power markets do not currently operate the multiday markets needed to schedule EV charging on a multiday to weekly basis using either hourly RTPs or an aggregated DLC mechanism. Second, the foresight value for RTP at 14% of LDVs participating ($31/veh-yr to $158/veh-yr) is of the same magnitude or greater than the perfect-foresight production cost savings ($41/veh-yr to $62/veh-yr). This suggests accurate forecasts of RTP response are necessary to achieve production cost savings once participation moves beyond early adopters. Finally, RTP, and to a lesser extent DLC, tends to increase maximum ramp rates as EVMC participation rates increase. As shown in Table A.2, RTP and DLC maximum ramp rates are higher than the unmanaged maximum ramp rate (3.93 gigawatts per hour, GW/h) at participation 14 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. rates greater than or equal to 27% of the LDV fleet for both within-session and within-week flexibility. To illustrate, Figure 4 shows the weeks containing the maximum single-hour upward ramps for the unmanaged scenario and for each of the DLC, RTP (perfect-foresight), and TOU (perfect-foresight) scenarios with 27% of LDVs participating with within-week flexibility. In this case, the maximum upward ramping requirements for the RTP scenario are 240% larger than for the unmanaged scenario. Although our envisioned ISO-NE system has sufficient flexibility to meet the ramping requirements for all scenarios except the most extreme one (45% of LDVs scheduling within-week flexibility against an RTP) while still reducing production costs, flexible capacity procurement and operation are necessary to produce this result. As shown in the lower right pane of Figure 4, the production cost model used in this study, which peaks at 31.7 GW, flexibly dispatches 14.2 GW of gas combined-cycle (CC) units, 271 megawatts (MW) of gas combustion turbines (CTs), and 858 MW of pumped storage hydropower to accommodate load spikes induced by RTP response. Figure 4. Maximum load ramps are greatly affected by the method used to dispatch flexible EV load. Within-week RTP for 27% of LDVs participating increases the maximum ramp rate 240% above that for the unmanaged scenario but still yields production cost savings (Table A.2).
